hypothesis: G01 = v2(n); G02 = v2(n)+1; G03 P-positions = odd numbers and 2^(2j+1); G04 = Omega(n); G05 = index of the smallest prime factor (and 'subtract k coprime to n' is the same game); G06: g(2k) = k-1, g(odd m) <= (m-1)/2, P-positions = {1} and the primes; subtract-a-power-of-k = the subtraction game {1, k}; any splitting game in which every heap >= 2 has an allowed split has g(n) = [n even]; G13 = popcount; G19 = floor(log2((n+1)/3)) + 1 (n >= 2); G20 = floor(log2 n).
methodology: Compare each closed form term by term with the exact values; count mismatches.
question: Do the conjectured closed forms hold on the whole computed range, and do the general structure theorems (power-of-k reduction, splitting parity) hold on new instances?
